hints: Look closely at the diagram of amylase. Notice it is not a straight chain, it is folded up into a compact, rounded 3D ball with helices and loops.
Remember which level describes the overall 3D folding of one polypeptide chain into a globular shape, held by bonds between R groups.
walkthrough:
**Observe what the diagram shows**

Look at amylase in the picture. You can see alpha-helices (coils) and beta-pleated sheets (arrows) all folded together into one compact globular molecule.

This is much more than just a sequence of amino acids.

**Recall the four levels of protein structure**

Primary is just the sequence of amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Secondary is the local coiling into alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet by hydrogen bonds.

Tertiary is the further folding of that chain into a precise 3D globular shape.

**Link tertiary to enzymes**

Tertiary structure is held by hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, disulfide bridges and hydrophobic interactions between R groups. This folding creates the specific active site of an enzyme like amylase.

So the globular shape you see is the tertiary structure, answer C.

options.A: Primary is only the linear order of amino acids in the polypeptide, it does not give the folded 3D globular shape.
options.B: Secondary is only the alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet formed by hydrogen bonding, not the overall folding into a globular molecule.
options.C: Tertiary is the folding of a single polypeptide into its compact 3D globular shape, which forms the active site of amylase.
options.D: Quaternary is the arrangement of two or more polypeptides together, but amylase function here is described by the folding of its single chain.
